rv.q: Instead, Steppenwolf Theatre Company is staging the world premiere of a predictable moral satire, which is of course not a satire at all...
In other words, one problem with “Adirondack Chair Circle” is that even the winning, and the losing, feels anti-climactic.
Adirondack Chair Circle is both funny and powerful.
The entire production is more validation that Steppenwolf seems to always know its audiences, even with accomplished satire that could very well have already happened here and there in America.
This is the kind of juicy uneasy theatre which Steppenwolf excels at.
Adirondack Chair Circle gains traction in its most energetic moments, particularly when the women address the school board at meetings with hilarious monologues.
For all its considerable virtues, that's the one thing Walker's play never quite delivers.
But Adirondack Chair Circle offers little to challenge the people already on its side, either.
“Adirondack Chair Circle” is a snapshot of our time, and it is timeless in its appeal.

This is a well written, nicely performed, thought provoking play that might have you considering how much control parents are entitled to have when it comes to ideas that might be considered controversial to some and how much we are willing to sacrifice for our cause.
The cast is so spot-on that it almost carried the day, despite the extra unnecessary hour in length.

cn.t: Walker's timely satire about book-banning moms draws mixed reviews: some praise its brilliant disruption of polarized discourse and sharp humor, while others criticize it as a predictable, one-sided strawman argument that preaches to the choir.
